title: SWE-Explore: Benchmarking How Coding Agents Explore Repositories
event_hint: New benchmark (SWE-Explore) released that isolates and measures repository-exploration capability of coding agents separately from end-to-end repair.
problem: Repository-level coding benchmarks such as SWE-bench treat coding tasks as a holistic binary prediction problem (resolved/unresolved), neglecting fine-grained agent capabilities such as repository understanding, context retrieval, code localization, and bug diagnosis. There is no standardized way to measure how well an agent explores a repo to locate relevant code under a fixed budget.
mechanism: SWE-Explore asks an explorer, given a repository and an issue, to return a ranked list of relevant code regions under a fixed line budget. Line-level ground truth is distilled from independent agent trajectories that successfully solved the same issue (the specific code regions those solution paths actually consulted). Evaluation is scored along coverage, ranking, and context-efficiency dimensions, which the authors show strongly track downstream repair behavior.

evidence.claim: Benchmark covers 848 issues across 10 programming languages and 203 open-source repositories.
Ground truth is derived from independent agent trajectories that successfully solved the same issue, distilling the specific code regions consulted.
Agentic explorers form a clear tier above classical retrieval methods.
File-level localization is already strong for modern methods, while line-level coverage and efficient ranking remain the key axes differentiating state-of-the-art explorers.
Coverage, ranking, and context-efficiency metrics strongly track downstream repair behavior.

evaluation_context: Benchmark of 848 issues over 203 open-source repos and 10 languages; ground truth derived from successful independent agent trajectories; retrieval methods, general coding agents, and specialized localizers evaluated on coverage/ranking/context-efficiency.
limitations: Abstract-level only; no specific numerical accuracy/recall percentages or per-method scores provided in the abstract (would require full text). Full body not fetched.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to Agent acceleration / code-graph tooling: it quantifies how well agents locate code in a repository, which is the retrieval/localization step that code-graph indexes and structural ranking aim to accelerate. Findings (agentic explorers beat classical retrieval; line-level coverage is the open differentiator) inform where structural code-graph investments pay off versus file-level methods.
